title: What a subagent needs, and where it should live
head: What the subagent needs
Changes per run?
Where it goes
rows: Material and decisions for this run (contracts, chosen benchmark)
Written in full into the Task prompt
Included completely in the next subagent's prompt
Role, method, quality bar that never change
rule: Subagents inherit nothing. Write everything specific to this run into the spawn prompt; keep standing instructions for what never changes.

title: Slow multi-agent run? Match the fix to the shape of the work
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Independent subtasks run one after another
Several Task calls in one response
They run concurrently; time is the slowest, not the sum
Sequence it after, pass the results in its prompt
Its input does not exist yet
Many requests don't need every stage
Coordinator selects subagents by query complexity
Richer explicit context in its prompt
rule: Independent subtasks: emit all the Task calls in one response. Dependent subtasks: sequence them and pass the results.

title: Should this work go to a subagent?
head: Situation
Right choice
Why
rows: Verbose discovery or long tool output
Small, dependent steps reviewed as you go
Delegation adds hand-off cost, buys nothing
Dependent task that is large and noisy
Sequential subagent with earlier results in its prompt
rule: Subagents earn their cost by isolating verbose output or running independent work in parallel. Without either, keep the work in the main session.

title: Subagent not doing its job? Find which step of delegation fails
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: No subagent ever starts; coordinator does the work inline
Subagents start, but the wrong one or none for certain requests
Subagent starts but returns generic or off-target work
Pass findings and goals explicitly in the Task prompt
Independent subagents run one after another
Emit several Task calls in one response
Subagent misuses a tool outside its role
rule: If no subagent ever runs, check that the coordinator can call Task before you tune any descriptions or prompts.

title: How should a coordinator be briefed?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Questions arrive in new shapes; the procedure breaks
Goal plus quality criteria; coordinator plans
Steps are regular and predictable, e.g. one pass per file
State what counts as enough evidence
rule: Brief a coordinator with the goal and the quality bar, and let it choose the steps.

title: Subagent output generic: what was missing from the hand-off?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Output ignores what you already know
Put the findings in the prompt
Output wanders in scope or depth
Say what to return and when it is complete
Need the full history, and the session has room
Explore subagent with an explicit brief
rule: Brief a subagent as if it knows nothing: give it the findings and say what done looks like.

title: Subagent output is vague: missing context, or missing input?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Vague output, and the task is independent of other helpers
Richer prompt: scope, dates, format, quality criteria
Vague output, and the task needs another helper's results
Sequence it after that helper; pass results in full
Several independent tasks run one by one
Multiple Task calls in one response
Helper uses tools outside its role
rule: Run independent tasks in parallel. Make a task wait for the results it depends on, and put those results in its prompt.

title: A subagent needs a fact: how should it get it?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Needs one fact another subagent produces
Coordinator passes it in the prompt
Needs many quick lookups during its work
Needs complex work from another role
Spawn in parallel in one response
Wants to read another agent's memory
rule: Subagents know only what is in their prompt. Pass a single dependent fact through the coordinator; use a scoped tool only for frequent lookups.

title: Subagent output weak? Ask what it was given
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Generic or hedged answers; facts are in the conversation
Write the facts into the Task prompt
Subagent needs backend records it cannot reach
Subagent understands the case but misapplies policy
Answers good but hard for the coordinator to use
Include complete prior findings in its prompt
rule: A subagent knows only what its prompt tells it. If the facts live in the conversation, write them into the Task prompt.

title: Subagent misses information: where should it be written?
head: Kind of information
Where it belongs
Why
rows: Changes on every request (committee rules, scope)
The Task prompt for that delegation
Subagents don't inherit the coordinator's history
Same on every run (role, method, output format)
The next Task prompt, in full
Two alternative directions from one baseline
Branches a session; not a delivery channel
rule: Per-request facts ride in the Task prompt. Fixed role rules live in the system prompt.

title: A multi-agent run is slow: what is the time spent on?
head: What you observe
Where the time goes
Fix
rows: Independent subagents run one after another
Several Task calls in one response
Many requests don't need every subagent
Running the full pipeline every time
Sequence that one; keep the rest parallel
Large overnight job, no one waiting
rule: Independent subtasks: emit all the Task calls in one response. Skip subagents only when a request doesn't need them.

title: Subagent lacks context: how should it get it?
head: Situation
Mechanism
Why
rows: Coordinator holds the specific facts the subagent needs
Write them into the subagent's prompt
Pass complete findings in its prompt
Ask or route to a person
rule: Subagents don't inherit context. Put what they need in their prompt.
